correctness.rationale: The Gaussian posterior variational infimum formula proves Loewner monotonicity even for singular spectrally truncated priors. The global error is PSD and bounded above by P, giving an operator-norm ratio at most lambda_1/lambda_(r+1). A scalar noisy observation with retained/omitted coefficients t/t^2 attains this bound as a supremum. Block-diagonal information gives no amplification. An algebraic rank-one difference yields the exact 2D threshold and a rational counterexample. The actual bundled verification program ran successfully with 385 deterministic symbolic and numerical assertions; all-dimensional universality is proved analytically, not inferred from testing.

originality.rationale: The motivating source implements a reduced covariance update exactly but does not bound reduced-versus-full posterior error. Information-aware low-rank Bayesian approximation was already developed by Spantini et al., including the qualitative objection to likelihood-blind spectral prior truncation; the novelty assessed is the exact sharp operator-norm minimax ratio, alignment dichotomy and scalar strength threshold, not the qualitative objection. Related ensemble error theory uses a different random sampling perturbation. No implication-covering statement was found in actual primary-text and mathematical-record comparisons; remaining full-text and indexing limitations are stated.

value.rationale: Low-rank covariance reduction is algorithmically motivated by large-scale filtering. The theorem identifies a sharp, potentially condition-number-sized gap between small spectral prior error and full posterior covariance error under one observation, while giving exact safe information alignment and a two-mode sensor-strength frontier. The exact universal constant and sharpness construction provide a useful benchmark beyond a routine isolated negative instance; the setting is explicitly first-update, finite-dimensional, and covariance-only.
